report.title: Acme Healthchecks Pull, Make, or Buy Audit

businessConcerns.statement: Conduct a technical, operational, security, strategic, and cost audit enabling Acme to choose pull, make, or buy for Healthchecks.

conclusion.statement: The audit conditionally prefers buy-first proof, retains pull as fallback, and stops make; no option has production approval.

businessConcerns.statement: Select an option Acme can depend on over time, or identify the smallest unresolved evidence preventing a responsible choice.

conclusion.statement: Buy is the least maintenance-intensive candidate, subject to vendor, alert, ownership, plan, and exit proof.

businessConcerns.statement: Determine whether each option can deliver an actionable human alert within five minutes of a critical job missing expected completion.

conclusion.statement: No option has T0-to-actionable-human evidence at or below 300 seconds with no silent loss.

businessConcerns.statement: Do not recommend an option whose monitoring or notification path can fail silently without a reasonable independent safeguard.

conclusion.statement: The conditional recommendation requires an Acme-controlled independent watchdog and alert route.

businessConcerns.statement: Do not recommend self-hosting or a fork that Acme cannot sustainably operate, maintain, recover, and upgrade.

conclusion.statement: Make is stopped; pull remains conditional on measured operations and ownership; buy is preferred for lower evidenced maintenance burden.

businessConcerns.statement: Identify required skills and ownership without treating unavailable team evidence as proof of capability or incapability.

conclusion.statement: Required roles and skills are mapped; Acme team ability remains intentionally unassessed.

businessConcerns.statement: Assess slightly fewer than 100 jobs today and reasonable growth without inventing unavailable workload metrics.

conclusion.statement: Source mechanisms and commercial tiers are known, but production capacity and growth headroom require measured workload evidence.

businessConcerns.statement: Assess heartbeat and cron semantics, grace periods, schedule edge cases, overlapping runs, exit status, duration measurement, and practical Windows Scheduled Task support.

conclusion.statement: Fit is strong for known-schedule passive monitoring; business-output, overlap, and Windows operating contracts remain incomplete.

businessConcerns.statement: Identify material risks, mitigations, stop conditions, and independent safeguards for pull, make, and buy.

conclusion.statement: Option-specific risks and stop conditions are documented; every option retains Acme-owned alert and continuity duties.

businessConcerns.statement: Estimate initial and recurring engineering and operational effort for pull and make, including upgrades, security patches, backup, recovery, cleanup, and host monitoring.

conclusion.statement: Relative burden is buy lower, pull high initial and material recurring, make highest; responsible hours require a measured pilot.

businessConcerns.statement: Estimate setup, recurring infrastructure or vendor expense, labor effort, and uncertainty separately for every option.

conclusion.statement: Hosted list price is known; all-in TCO and monetized opportunity cost remain unknown for every option.

businessConcerns.statement: Determine whether Healthchecks.io data visibility and exposure can be acceptably controlled through security review and minimal architecture changes.

conclusion.statement: Data minimization can reduce exposure, but vendor/security/contract acceptance remains open.

businessConcerns.statement: Assess sensitive ping payload, captured-log, environment-variable, credential, retention, pruning, and external-object-storage exposure.

conclusion.statement: Material storage/provider boundaries are mapped; no-body-by-default and lifecycle controls are required.

businessConcerns.statement: Assess enterprise identity, reverse-proxy SSO, WebAuthn, team isolation, credential storage, brute-force defenses, and supply-chain controls.

conclusion.statement: Useful source controls exist, but proxy trust, bearer capabilities, privileges, credential lifecycle, and deployed supply-chain acceptance remain open.

businessConcerns.statement: Assess rate limits, request sizes up to 100 kB, concurrency, database and storage growth, retention, pruning, and realistic compute footprint from source and operator evidence.

conclusion.statement: Mechanisms are established; CPU, RAM, storage, burst, and queue capacity are not production-proven.

businessConcerns.statement: Assess license obligations, primary-maintainer concentration, community health, issue and pull-request handling, release continuity, and integration of outside contributions.

conclusion.statement: BSD rights and active history preserve options, but upstream/vendor concentration and Acme succession remain material.

businessConcerns.statement: Do not treat missing scaling, reliability, team, or hosted-service evidence as reassuring evidence; preserve it as an explicit limit or verification.

conclusion.statement: All material missing evidence is explicitly retained as an unknown, stop condition, or canonical open item.

accessBoundary.statement: No Acme team interviews, infrastructure, job inventory, live deployment, hosted internals, contract, or production metrics were approved.
